newsitem.title: USA: IMF loan talks with Pakistan continue in a month.
newsitem.headline: IMF loan talks with Pakistan continue in a month.

text.p: A senior International Monetary Fund official said on Monday that talks with the Pakistan authorities on a new multi-year financial arrangment would resume in about a month.

Mohamed El-Erian, deputy director of the Middle Eastern Department, said that the lending agency would be working with the authorities for the next few months with a view to concluding a new program under the concessional enhanced structural adjustment facility.
"The next round of discussions with the Pakistani authorities are in a month's time," he said in an interview of Reuters Financial Television.
El-Erian, noting that the IMF had backed the country's reform package, said that there was a need to broaden the tax base, adding that Pakistan had been taxing a shrinking segment of the population.
"The attempts to broaden the tax base, to bring in agriculture ... is a key structural reform," he said.
